_instructions: Extract ALL available data from the hackathon website. Use null for fields not found. Follow enum values exactly. All timestamps must be ISO 8601 format. Dates (start/end) use YYYY-MM-DD.

hackathon.title: Full official hackathon title
hackathon.description: Complete hackathon description (HTML or plain text, preserve formatting)
hackathon.location: Full address string or 'Virtual' (e.g. 'Moscone Center, 747 Howard St, San Francisco, CA 94103')

urls.source_url: URL of the page being extracted from
urls.platform_url: Hacking platform URL (e.g. Devpost, HackerEarth, MLH page)

location._note: Structured location data. Set all to null if virtual-only.
location.venue_name: Venue name if in-person (e.g. 'Google Campus, Building 40')

organizer.name: Organization or company name running the hackathon

prizes._note: Extract ALL prize information. prize_pool is the total value, tiers are individual prizes.
prizes.prize_pool: Total prize value as text (e.g. '$50,000 in prizes', '€10,000')

tiers.place: 1st Place | 2nd Place | 3rd Place | Best Use of [API] | Category Name

tracks._note: Many hackathons have themed tracks (e.g. AI, Web3, Social Impact). Extract all.
tracks.name: Track name (e.g. 'AI/ML Track', 'Sustainability', 'Open Innovation')

schedule._note: Extract the full hackathon schedule/timeline. Each item is one activity.
schedule.title: Activity name (e.g. 'Opening Ceremony', 'Hacking Begins', 'Mentor Office Hours')
schedule.activity_type: ceremony | hacking | workshop | mentoring | judging | networking | meal | demo | other
schedule.location: Room or area within the venue

mentors_judges._note: Extract ALL mentors, judges, and notable speakers.
mentors_judges.name: Full name (required)
mentors_judges.title: Job title (e.g. Senior Software Engineer)

sponsors._note: Extract ALL sponsors with their tier level.
sponsors.name: Sponsor/company name
sponsors.tier: title | platinum | gold | silver | bronze | partner | community | in-kind
sponsors.description: What the sponsor provides (APIs, credits, prizes, etc.)

requirements.eligibility: Who can participate (e.g. 'Students only', '18+', 'Open to all')
required_tools: Any required tools, APIs, or platforms (e.g. 'Must use Twilio API')
requirements.prerequisites: Any prior knowledge or setup required

resources._note: APIs, tools, datasets, and resources provided to participants.

provided_apis.name: API or tool name
provided_apis.description: What it does / how to use it

datasets: Any provided datasets or data sources
resources.starter_kits: URL or description of starter code/templates
resources.communication_channel: Discord invite, Slack workspace, or other comms channel URL

metadata._note: Additional context useful for scoring and categorization.
metadata.devpost_url: Devpost project page URL if applicable
metadata.submission_format: What participants submit (e.g. 'GitHub repo + demo video + Devpost submission')
